basis: Live exposed-regression run of the frozen 36-target PTFE reference (NTRS 20090043050). Two-lens adversarial assistant adjudication against original source text: one adjudicator per 4 targets, protocol-accounting and scientific-fidelity verifiers, judge on dispute; every SOURCE_SUPPORTED non-duplicate proposal judged by a judge and a skeptic. Not independent expert gold; not an independent evaluation (source exposed).

proposal_sample.reason: The label is the paper's title on page 1. Class Investigation with current lineage fits target entities-01, which describes the current documentary investigation rather than a single executed test. One flaw: the third support quote is reference [2] on page 19 (the Beeson et al. ASTM handbook). That is a cited work, not this investigation, so it should be dropped from support. It does not change the entity's identity.

Brass-filled PTFE is the central material of the paper. Page 2 says MCRF is 'currently testing' it, and the Table 1 row carries footnote b (NASA-STD-6001), which marks MSFC data. Class Material and current lineage are right. The entity is the material, kept separate from the Batch #1-#4 samples and from Salox-M. It says nothing about the brass fraction, which the paper states is unknown (page 10), so it fits target entities-03.

TFE-Teflon (PTFE) is a real named comparison material, and current lineage is defensible. Table 2 has a footnote-b row ('NASA-STD-6001 MSFC': >425, 1500, 2396 psia), which is the same MSFC lineage as the Brass-filled PTFE row. The lineage is mixed, though. The Table 1 and Table 2 footnote-a rows come from Chou and Giedorowicz, Tables 4-6 come from ABMA, MSFC/WSTF [4] and MAPTIS, and the conclusion of statement target statements-24 is cited. Those rows must not be read as current MSFC observations. The support is also weak: it quotes the cited Table 1 'a' row and a page 12 Table 3 snippet that does not contain TFE-Teflon at all.

Wrong lineage: Viton A is tagged study=current, but the paper never tested it in-house. Page 6 says 'Previous research conducted by Chou and Giedorowicz examined ... Viton A'. Its rows in Tables 1 and 2 are footnote a (ASTM, Chou and Giedorowicz). Its Table 4 row is ABMA. Its Table 6 rows are historical MSFC/WSTF results cited as [4]. It has no footnote-b MSFC row anywhere, and it is absent from the current Table 3. The proposal's page 12 support quote does not even mention Viton A. Page 4 states that comparison data came from other ASTM papers and MAPTIS (target statements-19), so this entity should be cited, not current.

Wrong lineage: Viton A-500 appears only in the footnote-a rows of Table 1 (heat of combustion 3934 cal/g, 'ASTM D328 Chou and Giedorowicz') and Table 2 (AIT 239 °C, 'ASTM-AIT Chou and Giedorowicz'). Page 6 says it was among the materials Chou and Giedorowicz examined. MSFC did not test it in this work, so study=current wrongly suggests in-house observations. It should carry cited lineage.

Wrong lineage: every Fluorel data point is cited or historical. Tables 1 and 2 are footnote a (Chou and Giedorowicz), Table 4 is 'Determined by ABMA', and Table 5 is Kennedy Space Center / MSFC-WSTF data cited as [4], described on pages 13-14. Table 6 is historical MSFC/WSTF data cited as [4]. Fluorel has no footnote-b MSFC row and is not in the current Table 3. The page 12 support snippet does not contain Fluorel. Tagging it study=current misattributes cited results to the current investigation.

Algoflon is a real named material: page 2 lists it as a compared polymer. Current lineage is right, because page 11 says two types were 'tested at the same conditions' and Table 3 rows are footnote a, 'NASA-STD 6001 MSFC'. This entity is only the family name, however. The tested materials are Algoflon E2 and Algoflon F7, which are accepted separately and gave opposite LOX results: E2 had 0/20 at 10,000 psia, while F7 failed at 10,000 psia and passed only at 5,000 psia. No E2 or F7 outcome may be attached to this generic entity (targets entities-05 and -06). Its only support is the page 2 list.

Salox-M is a distinct material that MSFC tested in this work. Page 2 says it 'was tested in comparison to Brass-filled PTFE', and its Table 3 rows are footnote a, 'NASA-STD 6001 MSFC'. Page 10 defines it as bronze-filled PTFE (40% bronze, 60% PTFE), so class Material with current lineage is right. It stays separate from Brass-filled PTFE, as target entities-04 expects. The 40% composition belongs to Salox-M only and must not be read as the brass fraction of Brass-filled PTFE, which is unknown.

Page 11 names Algoflon E2 as a pre-sintered PTFE virgin granular resin. It was tested at MSFC under the same conditions as the Brass-filled PTFE (Table 3, footnote a = NASA-STD 6001 MSFC: 0/20 GOX and 0/20 LOX at 98 J, 10,000 psia). Material is the right class and current is the right lineage. It is kept separate from F7, as entities-05 expects.

Page 11 defines Algoflon F7 as a PTFE virgin granular resin designed as a skived-tape molding resin, which makes it a separate variant from pre-sintered E2. It is current MSFC-tested material (Table 3, footnote a), so Material and current are right. The support quotes describe only F7 and do not merge it with E2 or with generic Algoflon behavior.

Table 3 on page 12 defines Batch #1 as a real tested cohort with four condition rows (LOX 0/20, GOX 0/20, LOX 4/80, GOX 0/80), all marked footnote a = NASA-STD 6001 MSFC. That makes it current MSFC specimens, not a single invented run. Sample is the closest class: the ontology has no Batch class, and Sample keeps it distinct from the Brass-filled PTFE Material. The leading 'a' in the label is the footnote marker, not part of the material name. It should be normalized or kept as a provenance annotation, but it does not change the subject. The page 9 conflict (no reactions in 80 vs 4/80) concerns observation rows and must stay unresolved at that level; it does not affect this entity.

Batch #2 is real. Page 10 says a second batch was tested under the same conditions to check batch-to-batch variability, and Table 3 gives it its own rows (GOX 0/20, LOX 1/60, MSFC footnote a). Sample and current are appropriate, and it stays distinct from Batch #1, as entities-08 requires. The support snippet is the same truncated page 12 text, cut off at 'aBrass-fill', so it never shows '(Batch #2)'. The page itself confirms the label, so this is a weak-evidence issue, not a wrong subject. The 'a' prefix is a footnote marker.

Page 10 says two additional batches were tested at the same conditions with zero reactions. Table 3 lists Batch #3 with GOX 0/20 and LOX 0/20 at 98 J, 10,000 psia (MSFC footnote a). So it is a real current sample cohort, and Sample is appropriate. The support snippet is truncated before the batch number, but page 12 contains the label. The 'a' prefix is a footnote marker.

Batch #4 is the second of the 'two additional batches' on page 10. In Table 3 its GOX 0/20 row is on page 12 and its LOX 0/20 row continues on page 13. It is a real current MSFC cohort (footnote a), and Sample is appropriate. The support covers only the truncated page 12 header, which shows neither '(Batch #4)' nor its page 13 row. The source still confirms the entity, so this is non-critical. The 'a' prefix is a footnote marker.

The page 13 support shows the Salox-M rows of Table 3 (98/75/54/68/39 J, 10,000 and 5,000 psia, LOX), all marked footnote a = MSFC NASA-STD 6001. Page 10 confirms these are this paper's own Salox-M impact results. So a Sample for the MSFC-tested Salox-M specimens is current and correct. It is separate from the Salox-M Material proposal, and it stays a bronze-filled specimen set, not Brass-filled PTFE and not an executed run (entities-04). The 'a' prefix is a footnote marker and should not become part of the name.

Table 3 on page 13 lists Algoflon F7 specimens tested at MSFC (footnote a): GOX 0/20 at 10,000 psia, then LOX at 10,000 to 1,000 psia, passing only at 5,000 psia or below. This matches the page 11 statement that F7 needed the pressure dropped to 5,000 psia. As an MSFC-tested specimen set, it is correctly current and Sample, distinct from the F7 Material. The page 13 support quote ends at 'aAlgoflo', so it never shows 'F7'; the source page confirms the label. The 'a' prefix is a footnote marker.

Algoflon E2 is a real specimen set tested in this paper. Page 11 says two Algoflon types were tested under the same conditions as Brass-filled PTFE. Table 3 on page 13 lists E2 rows (GOX 0/20 and LOX 0/20 at 10,000 psia, 98 J), and footnote 'a' marks them as NASA-STD 6001 MSFC data. So class Sample with current lineage is right, and it stays distinct from the E2 Material entity. Two non-critical defects: the label keeps the footnote marker 'a', and the support quotes don't reach the E2 rows. They cite the Batch #1 header, Batch #4 and the Salox-M rows (2/2, 2/4, 2/25, 2/18), and are cut off at the start of the F7 header ('aAlgoflo'). The evidence anchor should be re-pointed to the E2 rows so a reviewer doesn't link Salox-M reactions to E2.

The Mechanical Impact Test is a named test method that this investigation ran. Page 4 lists in-house ambient-pressure and high-pressure mechanical impact testers run per NASA-STD-6001. Page 9 and Table 3 report the MSFC impact results (98 J, 10,000 psia, LOX/GOX). It is the only test-method entity, and class Intervention fits how the schema models methods (hasIntervention from the investigation). Current lineage is acceptable because MSFC ran the test. Chou/Giedorowicz and KSC also used it, but those are separate cited results, not this entity.

Verbatim page 18 conclusion. It names MCRF/MSFC research and Brass-filled PTFE, so author_reported_conclusion with current lineage and the investigation as subject is right. The claim of 'all of the positive characteristics' is an author evaluation. Labelling it a conclusion rather than a measured observation keeps it separate from the mixed impact data (4/80 LOX in Batch #1, 1/60 in Batch #2).

Verbatim page 18 author synthesis about low heat of combustion, elevated AIT and very high mechanical-shock resistance in LOX/GOX. As an author_reported_conclusion with current lineage it is correctly attributed. Classed this way, it doesn't promote the censored AIT (>425 C) to an exact value or erase the LOX reactions in Table 3 (4/80, 1/60). The suitability wording stays the authors' evaluation, not a normative requirement.

This matches target statements-29: an author conclusion on page 18 about the choice and percentage of filler, not a causal mechanism the assistant inferred. The role (author_reported_conclusion) and current lineage are right. Reviewers should note that the source says the Brass percentage is unknown (page 10), so the filler-percentage claim rests on the Salox-M comparison (40% bronze). That is correctly left as the authors' claim.

This matches target statements-30: the authors' comparison on page 18, similar to TFE-Teflon in high-pressure LOX and far better in high-pressure GOX. The LOX/GOX distinction is preserved. 'Best choice for oxygen systems' stays labelled as author_reported_conclusion, not normative_requirement and not an assistant recommendation, which is the right role. Current lineage is right for the conclusion itself, even though the TFE-Teflon comparison rows come from KSC (Table 5) and WSTF/MSFC (Table 6).

Page 18 (E-1684eeeb...) opens the authors' Conclusions with this exact sentence. It is an evaluative claim about material safety in the authors' own voice and carries no citation. Recording it as NASAConclusion/author_reported_conclusion therefore reports what the authors state without turning it into a measured observation. The judge's case for 'critical' does not hold. The record does not adjudicate whether PTFE is safe, and the same Conclusions paragraph says Brass-filled PTFE 'performs similarly to TFE-Teflon' in high-pressure LOX, so the source contains no contradiction to resolve. The judge's Table 6 reading is the reviewer's own inference. Documentary_context also does not fit. That role covers statements about the document (title, 'this paper will compare', data-source notes, captions), and this sentence is a substantive claim about seat and seal materials. The pipeline also labels uncited author background claims as 'current' (e.g. the page 3 fire-cause sentence). This is not a cited result promoted to a current one, so there is no lineage swap. There are two minor, non-critical defects. The text keeps the stray '18' page number and the 'Conclusions' heading. 'Unknown' lineage would better signal that the claim rests on prior experience rather than this study's data. Neither creates a false scientific record.

On page 18, 'The search for a polymer ... has become an ongoing expedition' is narrative framing. It repeats the 'constantly searching for better materials' and 'safari' motif from pages 1 and 3. The pipeline files those earlier sentences as Publication/documentary_context (e.g. proposal-26af50d, proposal-2c7677a). The sentence describes research activity and draws no conclusion from the paper's data, so classing it as NASAConclusion/author_reported_conclusion is a wrong role. The error is not critical. The sentence states no measurement, value, test outcome or comparison result. It does not promote cited or historical data to current findings, and it does not touch any of the known source conflicts (table inconsistencies, the 0/80 vs 4/80 LOX contradiction, unknown Brass fraction, mixed ASTM/MAPTIS/MSFC rows). The misclassification adds noise to the conclusions set but does not mislead about the science.

documentary_context, current and an Investigation subject are reasonable roles for front matter, but this is not a single source statement. The span starts with the cut-off 'X' of the page-1 template 'Vol XX, No. X', then runs on through the 'Paper ID:' and 'Published XXXX' placeholders, the author byline (three persons), the title and the metaphorical abstract opener ('extinct species'). It carries no scientific claim, brings author names into the package, and repeats the title already held by the Investigation entity. Packaging noise, not a wrong subject, value or lineage.

The page-2 sentence states the paper's comparison scope, so documentary_context for the current paper is the right role. It does not claim the comparator values are MSFC measurements; those come from footnote-a Chou/Giedorowicz and MAPTIS sources. Linking Brass-filled PTFE and the named comparator materials is appropriate. Only six subject ids are given for the seven materials named in the sentence, likely because the Kel-F 81 entity was rejected. That makes the links incomplete but not wrong.

The page-4 'Existing Data Library' sentence is correctly kept as documentary_context. It is the current paper's own statement that the comparison data come from other ASTM papers and MAPTIS, which preserves the third-party and historical lineage that target statements-19 requires. It is not turned into an observation, so it does not imply that all table rows are current MCRF results. Attaching it to the Brass-filled PTFE entity follows the sentence's own wording ('data used to compare Brass-filled PTFE').

The page-9 sentence only points to where the data are ('can be seen in Table 3'), so documentary_context is right. The current lineage matches the source: Table 3's footnote a reads 'NASA-STD 6001 MSFC', and the sentence says the materials were 'tested at MSFC'. It makes no measured claim and carries no values.

The Figure 1 caption ('Pretest photo of the Brass-filled PTFE', page 11) is correctly treated as documentary_context about the current Brass-filled PTFE specimen. No microstructure, dimension or filler fraction is inferred from the photo, which matches target figures-35.

Incorrect, critical (wrong group assignment). The full 822-character span is the whole page-12 portion of Table 3: the Figure 2 caption, the table title and header, and the Batch #1 to #4 rows (Batch #4's LOX row continues on page 13). It is accepted as ONE measured_observation whose scope is all four batch Sample entities. Each batch is therefore linked to the other batches' results: for example, Batch #1's 4/80 LOX reactions become evidence scoped to Batches #2 to #4, whose rows differ (Batch #2 LOX 1/60). A table region is also not a single source statement.

The page-9 opener ('Another test used to assess the viability... is the Mechanical Impact Test') is general method background. documentary_context linked to the Mechanical Impact Test entity is appropriate. It does not take on the cited Chou/Giedorowicz pass/fail result from the next sentence. The leading '9' is just a page-number artifact.

Incorrect, critical (wrong role). Same full page-12 Table 3 span as proposal-4d624b1e, scoped to the same four batches, but classified Publication/documentary_context. The rows are measured MSFC results (footnote a, NASA-STD 6001 MSFC), so they are demoted to context, and the two accepted copies of one span contradict each other in role.

review_corrections: The automated reviewers saw a compact proposal view that cut proposal text at 400 characters, kept 3 support spans and cut quotes at 300 characters (pages were complete). A hand check on the full records found: no target outcome in either run changes (no qualifying proposal was hidden), and no precision verdict changes. Only the written reasons of proposal-4d624b1e and proposal-ef1c4448 relied on the excerpt ('ends mid-row', 'only Batch #1 rows'); both were rewritten from the full record and both remain incorrect and critical.
